group_assessment.dominant_field: diabetic retinopathy (140 of 207 for the senior author, Kern TS); first author Saadane A has 36 publications, 1 on WWOX
group_assessment.method: PubMed esearch counts, 2026-07-26: Kern TS[au]; Kern TS[au] AND WWOX; Kern TS[au] AND diabetic retinopathy; Saadane A[au]; Saadane A[au] AND WWOX
group_assessment.weighting: Cuts both ways and the two weights must not be merged. WWOX arrived through unbiased label-free proteomics in a laboratory with no WWOX prior and nothing to defend, so the OBSERVATION is stronger than the same hit from a WWOX group would be. The INTERPRETATION is correspondingly weaker: the unsupported 'Wwox is a substrate for calpain' label is predictable domain inexperience, not sloppiness, which is why DIS-008 rejects the claim while leaving the possibility open.
group_assessment.honesty_note: This assessment was NOT performed during the pipeline run. It was done afterwards, only because the operator asked why the step had been skipped. legend-deepdive specifies group credibility as stage 1; the run began at stage 2. This manifest exists so that this class of omission cannot recur silently.
group_assessment.research_type_basis: Kern T S / Saadane A: diabetic-retinopathy wet-lab (in vivo mouse, ex vivo retina, Capn1-/- genetics, label-free proteomics, ERG electrophysiology, 661W line). First encounter with WWOX (1/207). Not a disease group; not a gene group.

field_density.verdict: The WWOX x calpain intersection is two records in all of PubMed. In a rare disease a near-empty intersection is a signal, not an absence: it means the edge is untested rather than tested and rejected. Also bounds the multi-hop debt at FT-020 to a tractable size.

multihop.note: NOT DONE during the run. All three are WWOX-direct and cited inside a source that was read cover to cover. Ref 87 underpins the transcriptional alternative on which DIS-008 rests, so the rejection currently stands on a source not read at first hand. Declared debt, not a closed step.
multihop.references_enumerated_basis: Europe PMC references endpoint for PMID 34214506; the PMC JATS deposit for PMC8579242 exposes no parseable <ref> elements, so the count comes from Europe PMC rather than the article XML. Backfilled by the PMID 22193544 session for schema compliance — the originating session owns any refinement.

corpus_crossquery.verdict: Calpain appears nowhere in the disease model except the seed corpus and the generated batch queue. The mechanism is genuinely new territory for this model, which is why the leads had to create DL-MECH-061 rather than attach to an existing claim.
